items.q: What should you remember about **Three-dimensional attachment map**?
items.a: **inferior parietal lobule uniquely tracks** changes in object spacing, sound timing, and emotional distance to people.

items.q: What should you remember about **Grief = uncoupling**?
items.a: **untangle attachment from space/time** predictions; episodic memory catalog persists and drives reverberatory seeking.

items.q: What should you remember about **Keep the attachment, remap space/time**?
items.a: **adaptive grieving preserves intensity** of bond; dismantling attachment is not the goal.

items.q: What should you remember about **Rational grieving blocks**?
items.a: **5–10–30+ min dedicated sessions;** feel closeness; actively avoid counterfactuals and guilt spirals.

items.q: What should you remember about **Kübler-Ross stages are partial**?
items.a: **fMRI shows motivation/craving circuits** (not just sadness) dominate grief; stages not universal.

items.q: What should you remember about **Oxytocin → yearning**?
items.a: **monogamous prairie voles have more accumbens** oxytocin receptors; human grief intensity varies by receptor density, not attachment depth.

items.q: What should you remember about **Writing disclosure**?
items.a: **35-subject bereavement study**: no group effect until stratified by vagal tone; high RSA writers benefited.

items.q: What should you remember about **Complicated grief cortisol**?
items.a: **afternoon/evening cortisol stays elevated;** morning sunlight + sleep hygiene as foundation.

items.q: What should you remember about **NSDR for remapping**?
items.a: **plasticity triggered by loss** + rational grieving practice; literal rewiring during deep sleep/NSDR.
